description: Check the health of a named vendor stack — a saved list of vendors representing your infrastructure dependencies. On the first call, provide vendors to define the stack; subsequent calls can omit vendors to reuse the saved list. Stacks are saved per authenticated caller, or per local server process; a shared deployment that does not authenticate callers saves nothing, so there vendors is required on every call and the response says so. Up to 20 vendors are saved per stack and checked per call; use several stack names for a larger set. Returns a unified health snapshot with an aggregate rollup plus per-vendor detail. A vendor that cannot be resolved or reached is reported in its own row and left out of the saved stack, so one bad entry never discards the sweep. Every vendor with an active problem gets a pre-filled devops_suggest_action call in nextToolSuggestions. Ideal for morning status checks or pre-deploy sweeps. Multiple stacks can coexist (e.g., "production", "staging").

component_filter.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against component names and their group names in detailed mode (e.g., "api" to check just the API components, or a product or region a page groups components under). Applied before component_limit, so it is the way to reach a component that the cap would otherwise omit. A filter that matches nothing for a vendor is reported in notice. Ignored in summary mode.

component_limit.description: Maximum components returned per vendor in detailed mode, at least 1. A value above 500 is reduced to 500, and notice says so. Large status pages publish hundreds of components, so a full stack at a high limit returns a very large response; narrow with component_filter instead where possible.

mode.description: summary: indicator + degraded components + active incidents. detailed: adds component lists and maintenance windows.

stack_name.description: Name for this vendor stack. Defaults to "default". Use distinct names to manage multiple stacks (e.g., "production", "data-layer"). Letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores, optionally separated by single dots or slashes ("prod.eu", "team/prod"); 1-64 characters. No spaces or colons.

vendors.description: Vendor slugs (e.g., "github", "aws") or raw Atlassian Statuspage base URLs. When provided, saves this list as the stack where stacks are saved; a list longer than 20 is then rejected and nothing is saved. When omitted, uses the previously saved list for stack_name; required on every call on a deployment that does not authenticate callers, which saves no stacks — there the first 20 are checked and the rest return in deferred_vendors. Lists longer than 100 are rejected.

items.description: A vendor slug (e.g., "github") or raw Atlassian Statuspage base URL.

name: devops_watch_stack

cap.description: The per-vendor component_limit that was applied. Present only when truncated.

checked_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of this check.

deferred_vendors.description: Entries past the first 20, verbatim and in order, that were not checked on this call: the rest of a passed vendors list on a deployment that saves no stacks, or of a saved stack holding more than 20. Resend them in another call. Empty when every entry was checked.

items.description: A vendor entry exactly as provided or saved.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `no_stack`: No vendors provided and no saved stack found for stack_name. `vendors_required`: No vendors provided on a deployment that saves no stacks because callers are not authenticated. `stack_too_large`: More than 20 vendors were provided on a deployment that saves stacks, so nothing was saved. `vendor_not_found`: No vendor in the stack could be checked and the first failure was a slug that is not in the registry and is not a valid URL. `target_blocked`: No vendor in the stack could be checked and the first failure was a raw URL resolving to a private, loopback, or cloud-metadata address. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

health.description: Aggregate health rollup: all_operational = everything clear, maintenance = at least one vendor in a scheduled window and nothing worse open, degraded = at least one minor issue, partial_outage = at least one major issue, major_outage = at least one critical outage, unknown = at least one vendor could not be checked (unresolvable entry, blocked target, or failed fetch) and no checked vendor reported a worse issue. Never all_operational when any vendor errored or is in a window.

nextToolSuggestions.description: One devops_suggest_action call per vendor with an active problem — an indicator of minor, major, or critical, or an open incident of that impact even while the indicator reads none or maintenance — with its arguments filled from that vendor's result. Vendors that could not be checked never appear. Empty when no checked vendor has an active problem.

items.description: A recommended follow-up tool call with pre-filled arguments.

args.description: Ready-to-use devops_suggest_action arguments: vendor (registry slug, or the normalized status page URL for a raw URL), vendor_indicator (only for minor, major, or critical), affected_components (degraded components outside a maintenance window, each written "Group / Leaf" when it is in a group), incident_summary (title of the most recently started open incident rated minor or worse).

reason.description: Why the vendor qualifies: its reported indicator, or the open incident behind it.

notice.description: Plain-language explanation of what this call left out or adjusted: vendors past the first 20 (listed in deferred_vendors), a component_limit above 500 reduced to 500, and in detailed mode how many components the cap omitted and how to reach them (component_filter to target one, or component_limit to raise a cap below 500), and which checked vendors component_filter matched no component of, with how many each publishes. Present only when one of these applies.

omitted_vendors.description: Entries that could not be resolved or whose URL was blocked; they still appear in vendors[] with an error. A call that saved the stack left them out of the write; a call that reused a saved stack leaves them in it until you re-provide the vendors list. Empty when every entry resolved.

items.description: A vendor entry that cannot be part of a usable stack.

persistence_notice.description: Present when this deployment saves no stacks because callers are not authenticated: nothing was saved, and vendors must be passed on every call.

shown.description: Components returned across the stack. Present only when truncated.

stack_persisted.description: True when the vendor list was saved on this call. Only the vendors that resolved are saved — see omitted_vendors. Always false on a deployment that does not authenticate callers, which saves no stacks (persistence_notice says so).

summary.description: Aggregate health counts across all checked vendors. Buckets partition the stack: operational + degraded + down + maintenance + unavailable = total.

degraded.description: Vendors with indicator = minor or major.

maintenance.description: Vendors with indicator = maintenance — in a scheduled window the vendor published. Counted apart from degraded and down, which are faults.

operational.description: Vendors with indicator = none and no error.

total.description: Total vendors checked on this call — never counts deferred_vendors.

unavailable.description: Vendors that could not be checked (carry an error) — unresolvable entry, blocked target, or failed status fetch. Counted as unknown, never operational.

totalCount.description: Components matching component_filter across the stack before the cap. Present only when truncated.

truncated.description: True when at least one vendor's component list was capped at component_limit. Absent when nothing was capped.

vendors.description: Per-vendor status results for the vendors checked, in stack order.

items.description: Status result for a single vendor.

id.description: Unique incident identifier from the vendor's status API.

impact.description: Severity level: none = informational, minor = degraded performance, major = partial outage, critical = full outage, maintenance = scheduled window folded into incident history.

latest_update.description: Most recent update text, as plain text: HTML markup the vendor published is converted, and any other < is text the vendor wrote.

started_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, with the vendor's UTC offset (Z, +00:00, or a local offset such as -07:00), when the incident started, or null/absent if not set by the vendor.

status.description: Current incident status (e.g., investigating, monitoring, resolved).

all_components.description: Components including operational ones, capped at component_limit per vendor and narrowed by component_filter (matched against name and group) when given. Present in detailed mode only.

description.description: Component description, or null if not provided.

group.description: Name of the group the status page files this component under — typically the product or region it belongs to — or null when it is not in a group.

name.description: Component name as the status page publishes it — the leaf alone, without its group. Several leaves can share a name (one per region or product); group tells them apart.

all_components_total.description: Components matching component_filter for this vendor before the component_limit cap. Larger than the length of all_components when this vendor was capped. Present in detailed mode only.

cached.description: True when this result was served from the 60s in-memory cache.

checked_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of this check.

degraded_components.description: Every component not in an operational state, uncapped — a vendor with a large edge-node fleet routinely publishes dozens. Includes in-progress maintenance windows (status under_maintenance) alongside genuine outages; read status to tell a planned window from a fault. Empty when all clear.

group.description: Name of the group the status page files this component under — typically the product or region it belongs to — or null when it is not in a group.

name.description: Component name as the status page publishes it — the leaf alone, without its group. Several leaves can share a name (one per region or product); group tells them apart.

status.description: Degradation level: degraded_performance = slow/intermittent, partial_outage = some requests failing, major_outage = most requests failing, under_maintenance = scheduled maintenance in progress.

error.description: Why this vendor could not be checked — unreachable status API, timeout, non-2xx, or a response that is not a Statuspage payload. Reported here rather than thrown so one bad vendor does not fail the batch. Absent when the vendor was fetched successfully.

indicator.description: Overall health indicator: none = all clear, minor = some degradation, major = significant outage, critical = complete outage, maintenance = scheduled window in progress, planned rather than a fault.

scheduled_maintenances.description: Upcoming or in-progress maintenance windows. Present in detailed mode only.

scheduled_for.description: ISO 8601 start time, with the vendor's UTC offset.

scheduled_until.description: ISO 8601 end time, with the vendor's UTC offset.

statuspage_url.description: Status page base URL used for this vendor.

vendor.description: Vendor slug or URL as provided.

title: Devops Watch Stack
